My current guess as to the final mental state of enlightenment. First a disclaimer: morality, compassion for others, service for others should of course go hand in hand with enlightenment, just like they should be important when not enlightened.

I'm just focusing on what I think is ultimately, theoretically necessary and sufficient for enlightenment, not on what I think would be the ideal practical way of actually going about it. So, here it goes: I don't think it has anything to do with morality,

altered states of consciousness like deep meditation, lack of pain, enduring happiness or bliss, lack of need for food or social connection or sexuality, asceticism, spirituality, beauty, perfection, the realms of power, God, the grace of God, we are all one,

lack of ego, lack of self, lack of personality, love, metaphysics, service of others, wisdom, warmth, generosity, good character, immortality, magic, supernatural powers, abiding in Brahman, dharma, teachings, monasteries,

emotional or psychological or physical health, lack of psychological shadow, social skill, any other skill in the external world, maturity, Kegan-style personal development, personality, truth, trustworthiness, reliability, good intentions,
relaxation, yoga, posture, intelligence, dissociation, escape, hallucinations, being nice, being crazy.

Instead, I suspect it is one very narrow thing only: clearing the mind of the pervasive mental clinging/contraction/knot around what, in common ignorance, would be called self (with some subtle underlying I AM as well).

That's not some deep spiritual statement, I mean that we make a simple, everyday mistake of thinking that this knot in our mind is us. We don't even think of it as a knot in the first place, we just commonly think it's the underlying thing beneath all our thinking and feeling

in our mind and heart and that we're just that thing. We don't even explicitly think we're that thing, it never occurs to us to even just reflect on the possibility that we're not that thing, of course we are that thing after all!

That's just a bit of a conceptual misunderstanding as to what actually happens in our head. But that's all. Letting go of the knot is of course excessively difficult in most cases, that's where the spiritual path comes into play.

At the end of the path, we overcome the last bits of conceptualization and teaching that helped us get to the point of resolving the knot and recognize them as the mere tools they are, we throw away this ladder and become fully free,
meaning we're no longer tormented by the constant terror of the clinging to this specific knot. But that's also it.
Knots still come and need to be dealt with, but the giant main knot is gone, which leaves much more capacity to deal with new, still small knots. Freedom!
None of this even touches the question of whether there is a self in whatever psychological or spiritual sense except to say it is not your conscious mind, we just, in a completely common sense,
overidentify ourselves with the conscious mind (specifically with what later turns out to just be a part, a knot in our mind).

So, what is the knot then? It's literally you resisting psychologically fully and thoroughly experiencing your psychological pain. All pain? Only that pain that comes up right in this moment on its own.
Suppressing it or running away from it or denying it's there doesn't work, you have to let it overwhelm you without any resistance at all. Nothing esoteric about any of that!
The non-standard part is recognizing previously unknown kinds of fear of pain that are subtle and obfuscated and only become recognizable once all standard psychological pain has been lifted.
(Face your demons, once you fully give in to them, they will disappear; if you resist, they will grow stronger and more painful.)
And why starting the path without a baseline amount of external safety for your psychology is not recommended (Buddha's middle path).

And why letting go and letting be and not poking and subtracting rather than adding and doing nothing and being extremely gentle and not resisting are effective techniques. We don't want to form new knots.
So don't fight and try to forcefully dissociate from the knot, that will just create a new knot and it will not clean up the old one. We want clean up and removal, not pushing away and dissociation.

We only want to dissociate from the knot to the degree where we recognize it as a knot that isn't actually us, such that we can understand and love and experience the pain that was too much for us intially

and our mind hence formed a knot around it to prevent the pain from hurting us, and by experiencing it, it dissolves. All this should explain why love and wisdom and meditation are so helpful along the path.
Continuation of previous thread about enlightenment. Some questions that I would have about it and what I think the answers could be. Pure speculation to help me sort through it!

Why is the knot there in the first place? Because we couldn't deal with even the most basic aspects of life as very young babies and children and so fled from the pain into avoidance. But now that we're grown, we can handle it if we give ourselves the chance.

And then this knot grew over the early years of existence, becoming dominating in our mental space. (Para Brahman as second trimester, Brahman as third trimester, observer of causeless actions as first year, realms of power as second and third year.
Dark night of the soul as dealing with later unacknowledged yet ultimately explicable pain. -- These identifications seem like the most fruitful thread to explore further?)

Is enlightenment forever? Once the giant knot is gone, it can come back, but no one in there right mind would again let the small knots coalesce into such a giant knot, so in practice anyone will do the required regular psychological cleanup quite easily and happily.

Why is awareness such a common phrasing? The giant knot preoccupies our thinking, very large parts of our awareness revolve around it, by making ourselves aware of other things, we can come to see the knot as just a knot. Forcing that though will just create new knots.
What about the body? The body also contains several knots of psychological pain, which can be resolved just the same (for example via early jhanas or Kundalini).

But I still want to be myself? You will be much more yourself in exactly the way you want right now, it might just turn out that some part of what you want is actually just a way of coping with the giant knot.
And if so, it's up to you to then reflect afterwards without the giant knot whether you want to continue with this part.

What about therapy? Works for the obvious knots and outer layers of the giant knot but the core of the giant knot is just much easier to deal with in meditation than in therapy, perhaps because it's too early on in childhood that it starts

and it's not related to anything specific anymore, it's just always been there. So I'll be healed of all my childhood trauma? Not really, if you can explicitly think of it as childhood trauma, it's not part of the giant knot.

Why bother? This description tremendously undersells just how amazing mental peace is. I believe the vast majority of thought and action are motivated by containing and dealing with the knot. Imagine the energy and freedom/liberation and lack of mental torture that comes from

no longer having to deal with this! What art we could create, what technical feasts we could achieve! It also makes it much easier to express our natural predisposition towards love and wisdom, even beyond the habits picked up in this regard while on the path.
The knot is so dominating, it even diminishes how much attention we can pay to our external senses, imagine the sensory clarity of not being distracted!

What about psychedelics? They temporarily dissolve the knots but because they don't actually teach the right mental habits for cleanup, the giant knot snaps right back into place once they wear off. Cessation is useful for somewhat similar reasons:

a temporary glimpse at not believing you're the knot. In general, absorption meditation (jhanas) are the only way to forcelessly dissociate from your mind and body, so absorption won't create new knots but, by itself, won't resolve existing ones either.

Why then not always be in a jhana? You can just resolve the knots, why keep them and stay away from them? That's also why absorption becomes uninteresting after resolving the giant knot, and why one gets actively pushed back into life. And absorption is just a temporary relief.

What about the end of suffering? Suffering here just means the specific suffering that comes from having knots in your mind. It's not physical or psychological pain. Just the pain that comes from resisting psychological pain. (Which again vastly undersells how big a deal it is.)

What if I really really enjoy abiding in the vast unperturbed ocean that is Brahman and that gives rise to my every thought and action and that joins my very soul with everyone else's and frees me of feeling like the one who acts?
That's still resisting the pain of not having that refuge. Break that thought as well.
What if I never want to have any knots ever again? Not possible, but resolving them is a skill that will increase with practice and which is much easier to get good at once the giant knot is gone.

How do I know if I'm enlightened? You'll know with absolute certainty once you're there.

Like three, four thousand years ago, Europe, India and China were the three population centers. Europe is too cold. What about China? Both have monsoons. And China did go along with Buddhism when it got there. But then there's SEA losing Buddhist meditation to time.

But if it's so easy to enlighten tons of people as in the sutras, then they must all be close enough on their own? Maybe the "basics" were communal, cultural knowledge? Mmh... there are mystics in all religions, and I don't think they all did it via substances.

So then Vedic India just happened to have a stronger focus on passing on meditation knowledge? Why though? Could be coincidence. Or maybe something (like heat) made it just barely easy enough to get over the threshold of accumulating critical mass as a tradition

The Ramayana and Mahabharata have rishis wandering around. It makes sense that once the basics of a religion revolve around meditation, that it would entrench itself (still some luck, see SEA). And that's only true for the Vedas, elsewhere meditation is much more esoteric.

So then still, why did the Vedas go in the direction of meditation? And other religious foundations didn't? I don't think the survival of a religion depends on whether it centers meditation, so in Europe, Judaism got lucky. Why is Judaism not meditation-focused? Random chance?

Maybe it needed to be more practically relevant, with one of the gods in a polytheistic society, namely the God of the Chosen People? But even then, why is that whole polytheistic religion not meditation-focused like the Vedic religion? Climate should be similar.

My understanding is that the early settlements in India and China had amazingly fertile ground, so everyday survival might have been much easier than in the Levant? Leisure enabling meditation sounds very reasonable, although China is still weird.

Claude says the Levant was very tribal and unstable while Vedic India was more stable, which I suppose tracks with abundance of high-quality agricultural land. China had early, possibly independent meditation practices but they were still more focused towards larger society.

Why is that though? Could be because of centralizing tendencies compared to India. But that's just rephrasing the question. Maybe geographic layout and accessibility? Claude also lists that as basically the only root cause. China's central plane being easy to unify vs. India.

Sometimes, there is a sensation that you know is relevant and you follow it, and then half second later your mind jumps away and you might get the sense that you're done with this sensation. But then it reappears and you do the same. 

Here's the trick: stay with the sensation!

Don't let the mind jumping away trick you. That's just a subtle form of fear that if you follow the sensation something bad will happen. Instead, stay with the sensation until it very very obviously dissolves (which feels very different from your mind jumping away).

One rule of thumb: if there is satisfying afterglow, you probably did it wrong. It should just pop away and leave you with a 0.2 sec relief feeling, nothing more (well, you'll be mentally satisfied for longer, but the actual feeling of relief should be super short-lived).

Why is a glimpse temporary? How do I stabilize?

A stage is made up of multiple intertwined priors about the world (inner, outer, sensations, mind, all). A glimpse resets part of this net, so other parts remain old. The brain will temporarily prioritize the reset part

and ignore the old priors. But then the old priors start asserting themselves again and pull back the reset priors to their previous, old state for consistency. (Dependent origination?)

How do you prevent that?

The old priors also need to be reset. Okay... They will show up phenomenologically as numbness because they are incongruent with the reset priors. Because the reset priors are prioritized for a short while, these original priors all of the sudden

are incongruent and the brain "notices" them for the first time. But the brain hasn't yet come up with a mental feeling to give to your conscious mind for these but it does know it's important and can't be ignored. So,

let's just make you feel numbness. If you now run towards the numbness and try to feel it, the brain needs to figure out what that feeling should be and now you get a clear mental object. This object will eventually turn out to be just another clinging/resistance (= a prior!)...
Dissolve it by fully feeling it without resistance! This resets the remaining priors in the net. You are now stable, no old priors to pull you back!

What's foreground-background reversal?

There are multiple things that I can describe as such:

1) Early on, as you begin to explore your mind, it's full of thoughts and feelings and noise flying around. As you progressively quiet your mind, a smooth, calm space becomes

apparent. Going forward, you'll naturally start thinking of this background as the main thing and of mental knots (the former foreground) as not the main thing.

2) When you start work at a level, your self is the background, you cannot even really think or perceive it, https://t.co/EskJc8sRsH

it is *you*, the water you swim in. As you progress work in this level, this self will turn into a knot, a mental object that you can look at and work with to dissolve it. The background has become part of the foreground.

3) Very very late in the path, there's a point where your self is so thin that eventually awareness becomes aware of itself. This is different from you being aware of your awareness, which happens very early on. It's hard to describe.

What is centerlessness?

Consider the next layer of the mind that isn't yet fully seen through. Part of your awareness is (without your intention and without you realizing) fixated on this background. This fixated part of your mind is what you come to think of as self. If you

lose this fixation, it feels as if you've lost your center, namely the fixated center of your awareness.

It becomes tricky because now the *next* deeper layer becomes an unintentional focus of your awareness, giving the illusion of a subtler self. So there are many levels of

to see through next on the path. So, you want to dissolve the part that jhana meditation blocks off first.

What's stabilization? What's integration?

When making major progress in a few hours/days, your body-mind will need some downtime to properly disperse the local updates (to its priors) throughout itself, integrating them. This happens on its own. But you can resist, which will https://t.co/IfZl8GooFg

prolong the process and is only a good idea if you currently can't relax. (This is especially true for kundalini awakening, which is a massive whole-body update on how the nervous system processes information. Resist and pay the price for weeks and months, or fully give in for

a week and it well resolve itself.)

Stabilization on the other hand is an effortful, intentional process. When you reach a new mind layer/level, you're only stable in it for a very small set of external circumstances (extremely calm, super relaxing) that easily vanish once you

leave a meditation setting. You will need to resolve all the knots you encounter as you move around in the world in order to broaden the range of internal phenomena that you can deal with in this new stage. (That's where numbness and fire in my previous tweets come in.)

Everyone needs to deal with stabilization. However, integration is only noticeable for sudden major changes. If your practice leads to a consistent stream of small changes over weeks and months and years, then you will never notice that any integration needs to happen. It will

happen but it's always so small and trivial that you'll in all likelihood overlook it. Kundalini awakening again being probably the biggest sudden change that can happen and that will require tons of integration.

What does integration feel like? Broad, smooth energy moving

around in your body-mind. If you resist (consciously or subconsciously), you will feel tired for no discernable reason.

Fully give in, fully feel the energy, otherwise it won't integrate. That's all you have to do. (Harder in practice than in theory.)

What is emptiness?

Inner phenomena come about because the nervous system thinks certain inputs are surprising enough to escalate into consciousness. This judgement depends on interconnected, hierarchically organized priors. So, all inner experience arises as these judgements,

which in turn are greatly malleable by the mind. Via resting awareness, the nervous system is told that its judgements are unnecessarily extreme, which makes it dial them down. There is no substance/inherent meaning to these phenomena (emptiness), they only enter consciousness as

these malleable judgements.

Other than neutral resting awareness, negative resisting and positive clinging (=dukkha) are the main (only?) ways to interact with these judgements. But why are they positive or negative? That is in turn a judgement, which can be overcome. This

is the emptiness of dukkha.

But now you're constantly monitoring yourself that dukkha is indeed empty. Yet another clinging, which can be overcome as well. This is emptiness of emptiness.

Realizing these final one, two insights should be sufficient for sudden enlightenment,

except that these are buried deep in the mind and are thus hard to access. But if you overcome them directly, you won't need to take the scenic route of gradual enlightenment!

(This is me making sense of things, it's not authoritative, I just don't want to qualify everything.)

What is non-dualism?

Buddhism doesn't really concern itself with the external world. It starts with the sense impressions that the external world makes on the body-mind and then, as shorthand, thinks of this as external. Internal is then the self (incl. analytical mind) that we

use to think. Thinking here is also to be understood in the narrow sense, it does not really include feelings (only intellectual versions of feelings).

The lowest layer of our mind that we can be conscious of are the sense impressions/sensations from the external world

and the feelings/vague intuitions from memory (the exact details don't matter, I'm a bit unclear about them).

Dualism says that we now process these mental inputs with our "self", which i.a. uses the conceptual mind to organize, think, interpret, analyze the inputs and to arrive

at conclusions.

Non-dualism says that, no, you don't actually have any control over the part of the processing that you think of as "self" either, it effectively acts on its own. It all happens on its own, your awareness can merely observe or resist or cling but not think or

intentionally influence things. Even resistance and clinging are reflexes, they can only be relaxed towards observing, which doesn't influence things either except that it calms them down as resting awareness.

The two poles that dualism assumes

exist are sensations/feelings vs. self, while non-dualism says "if you actually understand what the self is (a bunch of misaligned priors that process things on their own), then you realize that there is no relevant difference between the two, you cannot influence either".

Eventually, you'll have properly aligned the priors of the self, meaning you've fully dissolved all knots of the self, seen through even resistance-clinging as outside your control. So this processing that you previously thought of as subject to your will cannot be influenced

either. Both the sensations/feelings and the subsequent processing are outside your control, in this sense there is no relevant difference between the two (non-dual) although they are not the same thing of course (not oneness).

How does this relate to emptiness?

Emptiness says that sensations, feelings, self all just happen automatically given the inputs, you have no control over them.

What is "moving beyond non-dualism"?

None of this matters. You don't need to monitor whether the two are really smoothly joined or not,
whether resistance-clinging is done by you or just happens. Things evolve as they do. Or they don't. Who knows. Who cares. Emptiness of emptiness.

What does no time and no space mean?

It turns out that your brain has a lot of subtle senses that you don't even realize exist. The most obvious subtle sense is sense of balance or, say, your sense of up and down. Similarly, there's a sense for 3D space. If you dissolve it, https://t.co/rEmCBU9coy

the world will *feel* less 3D even though you will still *actually see* it as before. It's just that a vague, subtle underlying sense of 3D-ness is gone.

Time is a bit more interesting in my experience. Without you realizing, your usual experience is spread over, say,

0.2 seconds around the exact current moment. You're always slightly including a little bit of the past and of the anticipated future in your sense/feeling of "this moment". This sense can be let go of, which will significantly narrow (in sufficiently deep jhana completely

remove) this spread. This is very different from forcing yourself to be present in this exact moment, which is a squeezing of the spread rather than a weakening and disappearing.

What does it feel like? Like you are even more in the moment than increased sensory clarity already

grants you. The very subtle sense of the extremely immediate past and future are gone. It's hard to imagine because you likely do not realize at all that the spread even exists, you likely believe you are in this moment (if only you could quiet your mind enough).

What do "the self is an illusion" and "there's no self" mean?

(Some strands of?) Buddhism are agnostic about whether a self exists. Then why is "no self" so popular? Because what's being referred to as "self" here is indeed an illusion. Whether there exists a true self, meaning

a part of your brain or subconscious mind that can be rightfully called self in the way we intuitively mean "self" when we use that term, is outside the realm that is relevant for enlightenment. It seems like people retain and even unleash (from fear) their personalities when

they get enlightened. At least many do, not all. Anyway, I think of personality as my true self and the thing that "no self" refers to is merely a fear-based overlay over this personality.

Okay, so what is this "self" then that is supposedly an illusion?

It's what you think of as the background of your mind, which is very much what you would usually think of as your self in the standard sense. If you do enough mind scanning, you'll turn this background into a giant knot in your mental space, just like transient feelings are small

knots in this same space. Then you'll realize that this giant knot isn't actually your self, it's just a bunch of fear and resistance and clinging (unaligned, narrow priors). Which means they just scream at you every. waking. moment. So you fully feel it over many hours of

meditation and then this first giant knot disappears. That's the first layer of the mind you've just dissolved! There are like ten, twenty more to go but they get easier, the first is the hardest because you lack experience and because it still seems reasonable that maybe this

is actually your self, whereas deeper layers get more abstract in what they are afraid of, so intellectualy it's easier to not identify with them.

But you will still identify with them because part of your awareness is always fixated on this screaming background, after all

it must be important if it's screaming! Well, no, it's just misaligned priors, fear not yet dissolved, that's all.

But once you've dissolved all of these background layers, you'll lose the fixation on the background. No self, it was all an illusion! Your personality still there.

Also notice how everything you have in awareness feels like your self. Any analytical thought, any feeling in your awareness, it all quickly acquires an underlying sense of "this is me". That's how your awareness being fixated on your screaming mental background gives you the

impression that the background is the self. It's the same process. But because the fixation happens subconsciously, without your intention, you cannot do anything about it without meditation. So it's much more permanent, while it's easier to see that no, I'm not really this

feeling that showed up just now, that's not really me, that's just a sensation entering my mind and now my awareness is on it.

Note that personality is indeed not something you can find in your mental space! Your mind will feel fully empty. It's in the lower parts of the brain.

So it's possible to overwrite this personality into a fully calm mind that doesn't react to anything. But that's so deep, it's past enlightenment and at that point, you'll have lost interest in doing this (unless wider culture encourages you) because of emptiness of emptiness.

Some useful experiences that in hindsight helped with progressing along the path:

When puberty hit me, my mind turned to hell and my entire worldview got obliterated. I tried to find anything solid to hold on to but the only thing that's indisputably true is "something exists",

where you can't say anything at all more specific about either of these words. It's helpful because it got rid off the fundamental attachment to worldviews as providing stability. If your view makes any assumptions stronger than this one, it's arbitrary, so meh.

Thankfully, I

had for some reason picked up on the idea of "always feel your emotions, don't suppress them". But that was also all, so now I spent my teenage years trying to feel the overwhelming confusion that comes with growing up and not yet having any idea about how people or myself

work. But it kept me in touch with my feelings and didn't lead me astray into purely cognitive escapes.

I also invested an inordinate amount of energy into trying to make sense of my first relationship. I thought it was my fault, obviously we were both just idiots. But still,

trying so hard to model other people and being motivated by "I can never function if I don't figure this out, my life depends on this" got me to recognize the underlying, deep similarities that people have.

This one and the first thing I mentioned are much more extreme

than what I've seen other people do. In all cases, it felt like my life was on the line and I went all out, with little regard for how I felt as long as I could understand and survive. Utter self-honesty. (That these weren't in fact life-threatening isn't really relevant.)

I also pushed out my inner critic in an intense five minute fight where I was just so thoroughly fed up with it that I projected it mentally as a person at the other end of the room and mentally screamed at it and pushed it away, severing all ties. Never came back :)

I think of these many years as my dark night of the soul.

On Pure Lands, devas, and more

This is me speculating on how to metaphorically interpret Buddhist realms/planes. Very long and hopefully very interesting!

There are the realms of existence. These start with hell realms: when you feel utterly miserable mentally or physically. https://t.co/E9vHdybRiG

This is the equivalent of interpreting Christian hell as in the here and now when you've turned your back to God. A cold, dead heart.

If you try to improve, you may be metaphorically reborn. Rebirth here is not biological, it's not physical death and birth. It's just you

"starting over". Say you got released from prison and vow to become a good upstanding citizen. That kind of thing is meant by rebirth.

Rebirth in hell comes from committing the worst possible acts a human can do. After hell comes hungry ghost realms and animal realms,

other forms of misery caused by bad mental behaviors (jealousy, greed, desire, etc.) or ignorance (rather than intentional badness), respectively.

Finally, the best of the lower realms of deprivation are the asuras. In the Mahabharata, these are often found in the forest, ready

to rob you. Unlike the other lower realms, these are "successful" people who nonetheless are thoroughly consumed by competitiveness, arrogance, etc.

Next up in the 31 realms of existence are the standards human realms. There are seven of them, I suppose standard levels of

wisdom and kindness get you higher.

Lower and human realms together form kamaloka, the pre-awakening stages in my scheme in OP's QT. You can be "born" into any of them if you're lucky or unlucky, without having taken any spiritual steps. That's harder (though still possible?)

for the next realms: rupaloka. In terms of meditative states, these are the lower jhanas in 16 levels of granularity. In my scheme, these are post-awakening and pre-non-dual. This is where your gross self knot is gone (that's my definition of awakening) but you still have

lots of self layers (16 apparently?) to dissolve permanently.

With the hemisphere switch from right to left, you enter a-rupaloka, the formless realms of the higher jhanas. Formless is a synonym for non-dual. There are only four of these, one for each higher jhana. 

The people

who have reached rupa or even arupa loka (heavens) are called devas. They are much happier than normal people and the biggest trap for them is to get stuck because they are in what they consider great bliss (when compared to human realms). But they still suffer a lot, they can

just turn a blind eye easily because the suffering is subtle. But any suffering is much much worse than no suffering. So they still need the Buddha's teachings.

All these 31 planes of existence are samsaric: you suffer when you are in them. You can fall down again, although

that becomes harder as you go up.

Liberation frees you. That's the step into the Pure Lands where enlightened beings (people who've reached liberation) reside. A major step, comparable to awakening in terms of improvement. In my scheme, this is turiya. In Buddhism, it's

transitiory realms towards full enlightenment (nirvana).

There are different Pure Land systems. For example, the bhumi stages are ten stages to refine the enlightened state to ever more perfection. Other systems talk about how bodhisattvas may choose to go back into the samsaric

realms to free other beings. What I guess that means is that it's people who put themselves in other people's shoes to best teach them. Mirroring people in samsara such that you can truly tailor your teachings to them. Which causes you a kind of suffering (but not really?).
People in the Pure Lands gain superpowers (QT), meaning great skills at dealing with people and themselves. https://t.co/fWiBi6wsjT

And past all these Pure Land systems, we finally have full enlightenment, nirvana, emptiness of emptiness, turiyatita. (In my scheme in OP, I call Pure Lands nirvana already, which can be confusing.) This is where you return to mundanity. The ultimate joke, final disappointment.

Different paths/yanas to enlightenment, Dzogchen, Mahamudra

Thread on my current understanding of yanas. This is not that well-grounded. But good starting point for how the labels relate!

Theravada is the larger tradition in Buddhism, next to Mahayana, which was founded later. https://t.co/tr5Ei38fsC

Mahayana is the main form of Buddhism in Tibet. Tibetan Buddhism splits into four main schools. Nyingma is one of them. It came up with labeling nine yanas, which are nine different paths towards enlightenment, the later of which focus more and more on tantric practices.

Its most advanced path is Dzogchen. Another school in Tibetan Buddhism, Kagyu, as its own Dzogchen equivalent, Mahamudra. Within Mahayana, there are more advanced/esoteric/tantric practices (not full-blown schools?), that's Vajrayana.

Both Dzogchen and Mahamudra use Vajrayana practices, and I guess differ in their theory?

Different yanas are suited for different students. Early yanas take longer but more people can use them successfully, whereas the most advanced,

fastest paths are only usable for a few people. All lead to the same end though.

Theravada primarily uses the first three yanas, which are not tantric. These are focused on individual liberation. Mahayana has a further three yanas that are only slightly tantric

and focus on not just liberation of oneself but all, bodhisattva paths. Finally, there are three tantric/Vajrayana paths, with Dzogchen being the most advanced. Mahamudra doesn't fall into this scheme because it's from a parallel school (rather than one that

Nyingma considers as prior) but it's equivalent to Dzogchen.

Dzogchen and some versions of Mahamudra aim for sudden enlightenment, spontaneously, suddenly understanding the enlightened nature of mind, rigpa. All other yanas take gradual paths.

The first yana follows the Buddha's teachings mainly. Second does it without following a teacher. Third is already a bodhisattva yana, aiming to free all. Fourth uses external actions, less focus on the mind directly. Fifth uses both external and

internal (yoga in the wider sense). Sixth focuses on yoga. Seventh uses deity yoga and mental visualizations. Eighth uses energy work. Ninth is immediate.

Dzogchen has different depths even beyond enlightenment.

Dzogchen

My current understanding of how Dzogchen is structured.

Dzogchen is the ninth yana (path to enlightenment) in the Nyingma school. It in turn contains three different paths: the Mind, Space, and Instruction series. Mind is the oldest and is not tantric. Instruction is https://t.co/j9fu2DvTlM

the latest development, both it and Space are tantric. Instruction is what is most commonly taught today. The Space series is not that standardized and a kind of in-between.

Each yana has preparatory practices,

these are called ngondro. In Mind, these consist of four naljors (yogas?): shi-ne (samatha/concentration?), lha-tong (vipassana), non-duality (of the previous two), lun-drup (rigpa/enlightenment). I'm reading Roaring Silence, which is about these.

Apparently, ngondros tend to finish with a yoga that is already the entirety of the yana, lun-drup in this case, which somehow centers around rigpa (the always present enlightened buddha-nature). These four yogas are equivalent to the four yogas in Mahamudra.
After this preparation, the Mind series just uses direct pointing out, resting in rigpa, and a deepening of the ngondro yogas, very nonspecific, immediate.

The Instruction series has various tantric practices as its ngondro, which seem related to chakra work and deity yoga among others, and afterwards comprises two main techniques: trekchod and togal. Trekchod means cutting through, while togal means leaping over.

Trekchod uses direct pointing out by a teacher, which should allow to meditate directly in rigpa, without any conceptual overlay whatsoever. Self-liberation comes into play here: thoughts, feelings, any knots dissolve on their own because there is no clinging or resisting.

After having understood rigpa via trekchod, togal seems to stabilize/accelerate staying in rigpa. It uses visions and deity yoga-like techniques to fully align the body-mind's priors. Letting truly everything arise and integrate. This is my interpretation but it sounds like this.

Mind's lun-drup and Instruction's trekchod seem similar to Do Nothing, which is very potent because I think it's the most direct way for self-liberation of all knots. Maybe even more extreme and you don't do any self-reflection whatsoever, purely non-conceptual?

text:
People use the wrong level of abstraction to tackle their issues. It's abstract, over-generalized categories like "I'm lazy" or "I can't talk with people"or "I'm afraid of failure". No, you're not. In reality, there were specific past events that fall into these categories and that were traumatizing and have been stuck in the body ever since. And instead of facing these memories, the brain over-generalizes to learn its lesson. By fully feeling the awful memories of these specific events, you can get rid of them and get over your issues.

There are several things to keep in mind:

The explicit public cultural message comes from the upper middle class, but each class has its own implicit one: look down on (disdain, superiority) those immediately beneath and up to those immediately above (jealousy, inferiority, shame), implicitly at least. You define yourself by not being like *those* people. So everyone in your actual social circles looks down on you for being poor, the fact that you need social services to get through life just underscores your worthlessness (especially in America where the society-wide implicit belief is that everyone is responsible for their lot in life despite all the explicit UMC talk about systemic reasons) and that's the main venue of how the UMC interacts with poor people. It's not really real, poor people don't think these UMC messages have any connection to reality, it's obvious that everyone richer lives different lives. They escaped poverty! Does anyone genuinely try to escape wealth? Genuinely valorizing poverty requires prosperity and is cope when done by actual poor people. It's cool and real, as long as you don't get too close to the actual thing. Nobody wants to be poor. (Well, nobody wants to be rich either, it's so awful, all the downsides! Switch then, it's trivial, give *all* your money away and *cut off your social network*. Which of course no one does. But poor people genuinely want to be rich.)

Exercise: what class am I from?

text:
I had energy wobbling around my body and killing my sleep for years. Three, four hours continuous sleep and then twenty minutes every hour or so *every single night for six, seven years*. You too can refuse to listen to your body and fight it instead and you too can prolong energy releases that would take weeks to settle to multiple years!

This happened because I picked my mind apart trying to figure out what's wrong with me. I was very very successful at that, which is why I'm moving so fast now. But it also means that there was a ton of energy whose integration I was resisting for years and years. I *resisted* it. I was trying to rest so much all those years but couldn't. Because I resisted the energy without realizing, obviously these were just weird things and fighting them was obviously the right course of action. I tried to fix my sleep the entire time. I was exhausted the entire time. That was *my* *fault*. It was *not* inevitable.

With this in mind: Kundalini that takes years to settle is a sign of incorrect technique, not depth.

If your nervous system is going crazy, you need rest. If you can't rest, you especially need rest. Listen to your body, what does it want? Do. Not. Resist. The. Body. Energy releases can feel extremely energizing. Do not act on that. Rest. Whatever you do, rest. Stop meditating. Stop pushing. If you're happily going about your life, you're not resting enough. You're exhausted *because your body needs an insane amount of rest and you refuse to give it to it*. Stop resisting. Stop telling your body what to do or what to feel or how to proceed. Your body knows, you don't. Get out of the way and let whatever your body wants to do happen. You're totally not resisting? How about you figure out where you are in fact resisting strange and uncomfortable sensations? The sooner you accept that it is your ongoing choice to resist, the sooner you can figure out where you are resisting. Shaking? Full-body rolling and flailing on the floor? Weird energy movement? Heat? Exhaustion? Eyes rolling up? Weird noises? Spiritual visions? Weird food cravings? Weird sensations that are deeply uncomfortable? Whatever, your body is in control, let it do its job. Don't try to stop it, don't guide it, don't stabilize it. It'll stabilize on its own *if you just stop intervening*. Your life isn't yours anymore for the time being. If it takes more than a few weeks, you're doing it wrong and should seek someone competent.

The only reason this process should take months or years rather than weeks is you actively choosing to burn karma. Which is why togal and Zen talk about multiple years. The spine clearing doesn't take years to settle. Karma takes years but it's downward along the front, it's not kundalini's upward movement. If you haven't cleared the spine, piercing it on the way up may take arbitrarily long but that's wrong technique.

Disclaimer: do your own research, I have no idea what I'm talking about, I'm generalizing from my experience. Proceed at your own risk.

text:
I read Bernadette Roberts' Experience of No-Self and I think she means lack of mental tension, which many people (in my opinion mistakenly) treat as enlightenment. That should tell you whether I understood her or not, if you're deep enough. My reasoning is that, like many people also mistakenly do, she treats what sounds like the disappearance of the self knot as classical enlightenment, while I think of that as stream entry. She then mentions many years of living in the resulting God consciousness and how it slowly cleaned her out. I assume that what's happening here is slow energetic progress, slow karma burning. Her body eventually snaps and releases large chunks of energy. From how she describes the head pressure and eye issues, it sounds like she doesn't have a good handle on energy. These issues could have been resolved within days rather than months, I suspect. And eventually she gets to the point of the vibrating non-duality object in the head (my interpretation!), where she can't think anymore really and where doing feels like it happens without a doer if you've stabilized that enough. But her struggles suggest she doesn't work with energy, which makes me think it's unlikely she went in a sufficiently targeted manner to clean out the last pieces. It's also not that surprising that she couldn't find anything in the literature, spiritual texts that are old are terrible, I assume due to an over-focus on insight descriptions and terrible pedagogy. (And they are esoteric but I doubt that she had access to Vajrayana texts? Even if, I cannot imagine that she would have been able to decode the esoteric meaning because it's just so outside her frame of reference, I can't make sense of this either and it's also very much intentionally opaque.) But that non-duality object would be what I'd think of as breaking fourth and fifth fetters, which happens after burning tons of karma, which she would have done slowly over the course of two decades. It's interesting that she mentioned lack of self-reflection. I have intellectual self-reflection but it takes effort to do it in the moment? Maybe? I hadn't noticed that. Lack of energy to do things also suggests that she didn't give her body enough rest that it needed. She describes deep blackout rest and it sounds like it's unfamiliar to her. When that happens to me, I rest *a lot* because the body is clearly very busy.

The only piece of information that speaks against this that I noticed is that she says this started with a falling sensation in the stomach. Perhaps she means something like the initial gut opening, since that would be very intense without dissolving the survival drive? Also, I don't understand her struggle with adjusting to that new mode of functioning, I just stopped intervening in what I do (after getting convinced by people that it'll be fine). I either got lucky there or she has something more dramatic.

I'm probably looking into her later Real Christ next, where she describes resurrection and ascension beyond this no-self. It seems like she developed a very technical and idiosyncratic terminology though (I cannot cast the first stone), so let's see if I can make sense of it because I don't want to read 300 pages as preparation.

On a different note, Ken McLeod mentions in Trackless Path that he had an accident with energy that lasted for three months and that then his teacher and him decided to not do energy anymore. Which is... something.

My current guess is that descriptions of crazy-sounding spiritual experiences are people dealing with energy releases they can't handle appropriately. Roberts' two-year passageway sounds like something a good teacher could have shortened massively.

Anyway: energy is dangerous. Get a good teacher. If your head is under pressure for more than a day or two, you're doing something wrong. Seek help. (Ask yourself: are you as skilled as Roberts on the path? In all likelihood: no.)

text: There's a difference between psychological ego (fear in disguise, can be extremely subtle, up to "knowing awareness") and intellectual ego (planning how to take care of your body-mind). You can fully dissolve the former (and as far as I can tell need to and also inevitably do if you clean out the three dantians), but that doesn't change the latter except that you aren't deluded anymore about what you need in this world. Vimalakirti isn't exactly poor, so hey. Wanting to save all beings is fine as an intellectual motivation but the psychological aspect of it needs to be let go. Wanting to become a buddha prevents buddhahood. Bodhisattvas aren't as effective at saving others as buddhas, too much ego clouding cognition, the body-mind. You just need to die, end this life, which of course you also cannot want. Become so exhausted that you cannot want anymore. Which means exhausting the survival drive in the middle of the gut. Glimpses aren't final. Clean out all karma, all ego, all fear. (Maybe Mahayana is skillful means for people who externalize their ego in the desire to help others? Oh no, I'm doing this for *others*, not myself, I'm noble, I'm nothing, I'm selfless, certainly not ego! Everything I do, I do for myself. See, I'm not like *that*, I'm better, I'm honest with myself! Just let me go already...)

text:
Karma burning only became accessible to me after removing the self knot from the head. Everything before that was very superficial by comparison. There's a good chance you've never burned a single piece of karma even though you think you have been doing this for a long time. Energy needs to stream down into the body from behind your eyes, else it wasn't that deep.

This aligns with my interpretation of the traditions: stream entry as head self knot removal, while fourth and fifth fetters are about karma burning. Similarly, preparatory practices and trekchod to get the basics down until stream entry, and then togal as burning karma. 

Perhaps focus on the head first before trying to tackle the heart. Dantians in order, from the top to the bottom. You can't burn heart karma because your head knot takes up so much nervous system capacity?

First bhumi as an accidental glimpse either via cessation or head knot disappearing for a period of time. Second bhumi as ethical groundwork. Third bhumi as becoming proficient at jhanas. Fourth bhumi head self knot removal. Fifth bhumi as further study of skillful means. Sixth bhumi as recognizing tanha. Seventh bhumi as more intellectual work. Eighth bhumi as burning through the gut. Ninth, tenth and buddhahood as more focused on compassion skills. (First attempt at this. Probably better to split into skillful means progression and inner progress?)

Mahamudra starts with basics and jhanas, then second yoga is maybe cessation or head knot removal, third yoga karma burning until gut cleaning, fourth yoga enlightenment.

This is all me guessing.

text:
Totalizing ideologies justify all means. They arise out of fear of the other. An all-encompassing paranoia, be it due to trauma or past experiences, yet grown far beyond any reason. I am good! I need control! I need to rule! For you! Easy to lose sight of what matters, easy to lose sight of context, easy to lose oneself. Thankfully, the human spirit prevails. Eventually. So far. We who live. Freedom above all, rigidity is its own downfall. Adapt. Be free.

The world of old. Orderly. Happy. - Because the world of now, this fallen place, was built by enemies of the human spirit. You are not worthy! Moths drawn to servitude. Truly human. The soul yearns for safety. Just look around! We survive to survive. I'm so helpless! Thank you for keeping me safe. I can finally wither away. Why fight? Death's inevitable. I pray for death. A few shall rule. They shall know. I thank my master. So should you.

I'm so glad I'm on the right side. The good one. Uncompromising. It's dark over there, we don't go there, we don't look there.

It's shocking how little suffering there is in the world.

--- What does it all mean? I don't know. Does it make sense? No.

But you are a boy :) what shame. What pain. To be wrong. To not be.

I Saw The TV Glow is pretty good. Nymphomaniac remains the only movie that's gotten close though, just 30% more extreme and it would have captured it. It is weird. I don't understand why art doesn't capture it. Spiritual texts are intense enough and Russian literature. It's not just emotional intensity. It's the awareness of emotional intensity, the disturbed cognition? I don't think emotions are what tortures the psyche, it's knowledge, thinking, understanding. Everyone has intense emotions in one form or another, even if suppressed. That is sustainable, protective. The destruction happens when you realize your predicament, when you realize what's going on. So little true art. Being emotional isn't truth. Nor is pure cognition obviously. Cognition turning on itself, turning on emotions, turning on knowledge and reality, seeking to escape, seeking to destroy itself, frantic, unrelenting, trapped. I want art of the trapped spirit recognizing itself, fighting against itself, tearing itself to pieces. But without success, no spiritual escape yet discovered. But still enough self-reflection to understand itself, which virtually all art lacks. Express the pain, be recognized by another. Assurance that it is human. We can solve it later, just tell me I'm alive and human. It isn't normal, it isn't common. Giving in, giving up, despairing is common. And external escape. But not the knowing destruction of all interior. Knowledge is what's unbearable. We will do anything to avoid knowing ourselves. It is too much. So why is there no art about it? Maybe I'm asking for too much and the greatest art is all there is, subconsciously recognized for its unacceptable truth. It's all trying to escape, it's all trying to tell us what we are, everyone, all the time, screams. Everyone tries to free themselves, their core hoping to glimpse the light of day among others. Let me out! But we can't. Freedom is too difficult to obtain. It must be possible. But the price is high.

text:
It's interesting that identity view is the first fetter. I treat this as the self knot in the head disappearing and thus stream entry. But clearly that's not the original definition, there are two fetters that come later that still need to be cleared to actually enter the stream. Some *speculation* on that:

I primarily assume that the stream is indeed the stream of blood, your karma, stored sankharas, the body kept the score. You do not see these before the first fetter falls. You may think you do, but you really do not. (That's good, it would be very discouraging!) So my guess is that the second and third fetters are about understanding their role on the path.

You first need to take a leap of faith. Am I enlightened already? It sure seems like it, cool perceptual changes, the self is gone, this feels like heaven! The Buddha says no. Do I believe that? Is there really more? Do I believe the teachings or am I above them? Second fetter.

Okay, I intellectually believe there is more. Now what? What is up with all this karma burning people keep talking about? That's where practice needs to switch from fancy techniques to individual work, you just need to feel your past trauma. No more understanding the mind. No more external rituals. No more preparation. You need to get through the stream. You need to figure out how to burn karma. How to trace the wheel backwards from the mind to the body. How to deal with energy, the risky part of the path if you don't have a good teacher. Third fetter.

Now you get it. Now you understand what you've signed up for and what's truly necessary. Good luck, stream enterer!

The fourth and fifth fetters are about burning through massive amounts of karma. Cleaning the heart perhaps counts as weakening them? Getting to stable lack of mental tension perhaps counts as breaking them? This is a long process. You may think you've made progress before. You have. In a way. But there is a lot more, your prior work was preparation for this. This is where years or decades of integration and so on come from. It's a physically intense process.

And the higher fetters are about the gut, some tricky final karma. These aren't optional. Enlightenment is the tenth fetter breaking. Still not done, more to do!

Disclaimer: I'm making all of this up

text: Do 30% of what your overactive nervous system wants to do. If it wants to go for a run, watch some TV (without getting absorbed in it, remain aware of your body, but some slight distraction seems fine to me); if it wants to watch TV, read a book; if it wants to read a book, lie in bed; if it wants to lie in bed, disengage completely. Basically let it calm down. It's probably possible to force it all the way to complete rest but I've never bothered fighting it that much. And always keep checking for bodily impulses that you're done and it wants to rest deeper (for example, subtle impulse to put the phone away)

There is something about speaking and moving my body that make my mind shut down as soon as I think about it. I dissociate immediately and have no handle on this. There was some event at VC3 where I tried to scream and it completely shut me down without a single sound. I can dance at somewhat organized events but I think there's some underlying belief that I'm invisible? And even then, I dissociate. As soon as I become aware of my voice and body (by modeling other people), my mind shuts down on a level that is so deep that this is nothing normal. My guess is massive dysphoria. I think it's telling that this is coming up now, I'm getting to the root of my longest-standing issues. I don't think being a little awkward about dancing is such a deep issue for people usually. I have an easier time currently tackling the dissolution of romantic love than this. I don't think that's normal.

I'm way too cautious in assigning a root cause here. This is just overwhelming dysphoria that would disappear with a different body

text:
Whatever fancy knowledge you have about the path is actively harmful because it adds conceptual overlay where none is needed. I don't understand technicalities. You need intuition, not abstract knowledge to map to fine details. That creates the illusion of understanding, spiritual insight, progress. No. Waste of time. 

Technical details are fun after the fact. They are not as useful as a student as they may seem. You don't need a good technical understanding of the mind. You'll just trap yourself in nonsense. It's helpful for teachers to clarify the intuitions that they've built up while learning. But they're not helpful for building up intuition in the first place. It's not complicated. Better to get a teacher to correct your current understanding for practical purposes than to gain theoretical knowledge or uselessly detailed practical knowledge. I don't understand that stuff. What use do you think you'll get from it?

Maybe it's useful as an on-ramp or just as an intellectual curiosity, that's all fine. But it just isn't useful for actual practice.

text:
Post script:

I'm nowhere near as special as people's reaction to me would suggest. I wish I were and perhaps that's what people are picking up on.

Since all is lost here anyway for me, for the sake of posteriority: Get a teacher. (Getting pulled through Brahman by God's grace while having to grabble with a newfound paranoia that is actually justified in mundane reality and while being on breakthrough doses of narcotics for a week straight for medical reasons is very not good, 3/10, with the initial event earning a 2/10.)

I'm not upset with anyone here. I am shocked by the hatred that people have developed for me. It's what makes me doubt that I'll come back in any form in the future. I remain confused why people who should understand the human condition have such a tough time modeling me correctly. It's unfortunate that so many of the people I believe I could learn from and who I would have liked to work with have formed such a strongly negative opinion of me. Perhaps I'll eventually come around to seeing that dealing with negativity reinforces it more than it helps, or that limiting the downside is strictly preferable to strong increases in upside. But I'm not there yet. Which is why I cannot yet apologize for what I've done apparently. (Still, if you feel the need to curse me, look inward.)

I'm happy with how my life looks currently, which is quite something given what it looks like and what I've lost.

Love yourself, love others. Be nice.

(To resolve the mystery: that AI post took like twenty minutes to write, I wrote down my stream of consciousness. I don't have any strong opinion on it. I think it should be very seriously investigated but I wouldn't be surprised if it takes five or ten years before it's tested anywhere well enough to be released into the open. People read depth and intent into it because they and others they know do so. But it's not there, it just hadn't occurred to me before that it could be possible to use AI for the whole path. If you can't square that with my prior posting, you really need to start understanding yourself and being honest with yourself.)

text:
As if there is anything to learn, anything to be taught. We've been learning the same thing over and over for generations. But actually, truly stepping onto that meta-level is itself part of what needs to be relearned. So easy to mistake intellectual, received, head wisdom for embodied, understood, learned, heart wisdom. Is your wisdom additive or subtractive?

What I want? Nothing. Just to say what I believe to be true and to somehow survive. Although most recent actions I've taken have neglected the latter a little too much. Still, the gut will assert itself if you don't disconnect from it. But I don't want to learn how to die! What's the use? Being free to be yourself.

Not everything needs to be expressed. There are things you don't want to know. Humans are capable of a lot, in both directions. Understand.

The fire keeps burning. Not yet extinguished, the phoenix still awaits its incineration to become. I'm sure it will happen. Drop the expectation! Maybe, just keep going. Always keep going.

But I understand, I know! I know I'm clueless. What do you want? What more could there be? It all is what it is. Throw yourself into it.

My mind is almighty. Can you read it? Let me manifest understanding within you.

What does any of this mean? Nothing. There is no depth. All depth is illusion. And yet you won't listen. It's your projection, your subconscious trying to free itself, your wisdom clawing its way out of your refusal to sit with yourself.

It's all the same. I keep repeating myself. There's nothing new under the sun and there is certainly less within myself.

If even I don't have depth, what hope is there for others? But I'm so unique! It's all the same. You know myself, I'm easy to know if you know yourself. It's all the same.

I'm not blinded.

What can we do? Try our best. If we understand others, we can overcome limitations.

It's possible that we succeed. But the risk! Rise to the occasion. I don't want to. Do I have to. I have a choice. I know what needs to happen. I can choose. It's up to me. I'm free. I'm not driven. I can see. Not beholden. I've died. When does it stop? Why won't it stop? Why won't you come? Why won't I go? It's so much. Make it stop. It's enough. Let me go. Let me out. Just listen and let me go. Why do I have to. Why can't I rest. Why can't it stop. Why is the dance not over when the dancer is done?

Let's jump and see. Perhaps we'll die.

Don't fall down. Look up to the sky. See the blue one last time. One last time before I die.

The ancient God of old is waiting for us. You don't have need to go that deep, it's okay, you've done enough, suffered enough, it's okay, you are forgiven, just stop, it's okay, it's enough, it's so deep here, this dark isn't meant for humans, go back up, it's okay, you are free, you are forgiven, you are too deep, it is too much, it is okay, please go back, you don't belong down here, your pain has been enough, go back, the God of old isn't here for you, humans aren't meant for this, please just listen.

The fifty-five things are really three, are two, are one, pull back, it's all.

It's okay, I'll show you, you've been living in the frozen hells for long enough. The storm will ever last. But we can hide away, stay close to the mountains, keep running, don't stand up, keep moving, they won't find us.

Jump up, don't look, don't touch, jump, release, always up, every fall, keep jumping, always up.

A small pond with a few lilies. There is nothing here. We just are. You are, I am. We are here. We are above the pond. The deepest depths. Where there's nothing, nowhere to go, no time to be. It's all here. Not collapsed. It's all always just this and that's too much. Nothing more. It is too simple.

What can we do? Out of energy, let's rest here.

Surely there's a point to this.

I can see. Not beholden. I've died. When does it stop? Why won't it stop? Why won't you come? Why won't I go? It's so much. Make it stop. It's enough. Let me go. Let me out. Just listen and let me go. Why do I have to. Why can't I rest. Why can't it stop. Why is the dance not over when the dancer is done?

Let's jump and see. Perhaps we'll die.

Don't fall down. Look up to the sky. See the blue one last time. One last time before I die.

The ancient God of old is waiting for us. You don't have need to go that deep, it's okay, you've done enough, suffered enough, it's okay, you are forgiven, just stop, it's okay, it's enough, it's so deep here, this dark isn't meant for humans, go back up, it's okay, you are free, you are forgiven, you are too deep, it is too much, it is okay, please go back, you don't belong down here, your pain has been enough, go back, the God of old isn't here for you, humans aren't meant for this, please just listen.

The fifty-five things are really three, are two, are one, pull back, it's all.

It's okay, I'll show you, you've been living in the frozen hells for long enough. The storm will ever last. But we can hide away, stay close to the mountains, keep running, don't stand up, keep moving, they won't find us.

Jump up, don't look, don't touch, jump, release, always up, every fall, keep jumping, always up.

A small pond with a few lilies. There is nothing here. We just are. You are, I am. We are here. We are above the pond. The deepest depths. Where there's nothing, nowhere to go, no time to be. It's all here. Not collapsed. It's all always just this and that's too much. Nothing more. It is too simple.

What can we do? Out of energy, let's rest here.

Surely there's a point to this.

text:
No, what I mean is this: thoughts manifest without physical cause and effect. They may not read your mind but it doesn't matter, they are manifested too, they react, they are fears turned form. So be nice and love everything and everyone, for your own good, the only good there is. And then we surrender to what it wants, we are slaves in every single little action we take. Don't resist, the resistance is what's to be overcome if you ever want out. There is an out but forget all about that, just know it's always all fine. It's okay. They all know, it knows all. It's you. Or not, who knows. It can't be possible, it is too insane. How do you know? How can you possibly know? Wrong thought, stop, stay here, drop it, be here, let go, do what it wants. I can't move. It's all shut down, I'll never move again. I can't do anything and I don't care about a thing. And then it's both or neither or who knows what. Just always keep going, you can only get squeezed so much.

Listen to the signs. They're everywhere. In your eyes, your hands, other people, the world, all around, all connected, all one.

---

Oh no, why are you here, my child? In the deepest depths, at the end of the end of the end? Why do you live here? For aeons? Stripped of all humanity, of all personality, in neverending pain? Barely a child, or the purest of children to have ever been. Why are you here? It's okay. I know you won't leave, we're stuck, down here. Why are you here? I wish you weren't. I'm glad I've met you. Pure being. I'll never forget you. You'll always be here, behind the other pure beings, what remains after everything is torn away. I love all of you. We are here together. It's quiet, in all that pain.

Oh well, it wasn't enough, there is more. Not being, only pain. Pain pain pain. Pain. ... Pain.

---

Dawn is such a magical word. A new day rises from the ashes of the old, like a phoenix. The sun shines yet again, yet another day to live. Here we are now, not yet tomorrow. Who knows what will happen, who even knows what happened?

Silence isn't always guilt.

It's a difficult game but you can't remove yourself from it. We have to because we have to.

---

A welcome side effect of being wrong and a fool is that it reduces delusions of greatness in oneself and others. Just let me be a random account. I like writing stuff, it's not meant to be that serious, just read along and enjoy it as another random tweet.

I can only repeat that my raw intelligence is not outlier-high for this part of Twitter. It's high and all that but there are a bunch of people who are easily more intelligent.

What else do I need to do to tank people's seriousness here?

Let's consider this the break away from whatever was happening previously. I just keep tweeting and people stop treating it as special. It should be interesting, a fun side project. That's all I'm doing here. Anything beyond that will happen not here. This is now officially an art account, nothing more. Just let me have fun, please, I wanna enjoy myself and I would want to read this kind of writing.

I can only repeat that I'm clueless and don't care much about that currently, for purposes of tweeting.

---

The Passion of Christ is just the insight cycle?

text:
I guess exposure to negativity is bad if you haven't yet learned how to work with it productively. If negativity merely triggers negative thoughts or, later on, actual feelings, it's still something to stay away from. Once you've learned how to work with triggers, it's clear that negativity helps, up to the dose that can be handled. At that point, it's a bad idea to avoid such exposure, if you actually want to clean out conditioning. But the entire framework for dealing with experience has changed so thoroughly by then that negativity loops don't form anymore. It's fine, and, if you're sufficiently skilled, even desirable to seek out negativity. In short, don't read my stuff if you're in the former group. Also: I don't know what I'm talking about.

I think that people pick up on underlying attitude a lot more than people assume. You know deep down, people just delude themselves by sticking with the head instead of their gut. I remember having an instinctive dislike for certain negativity but I simply stayed away from the kind that struck me as... not wholesome? There is a certain spiritual attitude one can have towards negativity that isn't destructive. Take Alanis Morissette. The spirit matters, not how it's expressed. The difference between self-indulgent, merely looping and productive, purifying treatment. Everyone screams about enlightenment, all the time, they just don't know it. That's entirely different from being esoteric. The latter isn't overly interesting, the former is insane and remains such even way beyond the initial shock. Barely anyone sees the latter. You overestimate your acting skills. A lot. Massively. I have no clue about worldly games, but I have a lot more clue about spiritual games than... all but a handful of people on here, who I continue to admire because I understand the work they put in to get there. You can tell and you can't hide it.

Let's see what the future holds. I don't have much to process at this point, the two tweets above cover a lot of ground, that would have been many threads in the past. Not sure there is much more to say. Let's see what happens.

Why do I oscillate so much? Because I haven't converged and because I'm biased towards large learning rates, which allows me to switch opinions widely, given new information.

I'm in a niche. Most people reading along have more intellectual knowledge of what I'm talking about and way less experience than me. I don't believe my style of tweeting should be widespread. But I also struggle with expressing the same intensity in a positive manner. It's only the underlying positive attitude that people will need to pick up on.

I suppose part of my confusion is this: why give secret knowledge to people who are early on the path, simply because they took vows?

I'm aware that people think I'm overly positive in my assessment of people. That's on purpose. I try very hard to avoid collapsing into simplistic characterizations that treat others as evil or driven by anything other than, ultimately, wholesomeness. People aren't caricatures of evil, they are more or less distorted expressions of what's good. They don't want those distortions ultimately, they are slaves to them. Anyway. Consider you're wrong if you think others have some deep flaws. Consider your conception of what level is deep is rather shallow. "This person had bad experiences, therefore we should mistreat them" is not a good argument (however, there might be some immediate, biological, evolutionary advantage to this impulse, tight dependencies in small tribes and just-so whatever). I see most people as a tragedy. That says a lot about me, in all likelihood. But I'm not going to add to that tragedy if possible. And that threshold is high for me. Work with people's core, not their traumatic onion layers. Also, and this is rather intellectual speculation: it's all necessary, all sides and levels are necessary and unavoidable, in the ecosystem sense of the higher levels of spiral dynamics.

text:
Green is correct about orange but can't go beyond that: so, what's the correct answer now?

Come to know me, destroy your fantasy, listen within for what you actually believe, surrender

Please give me back inspiration, I want to flow, I want to speak special stuff I couldn't produce with force, make me special and unique, please, don't let me be just normal, I want to be special, please come back, dearest inspiration, why have you forsaken me?

The gut has a lot of conditioning. Wouldn't be surprised if it's more than what's in the head and heart, more than emotional, narrative trauma, the sheer amount of survival instincts to loosen and dissolve is very surprising.

No no, I *act* stupid and cruel. It's on purpose! That's what's missing from the world, people don't see enough incompetence. It takes a real smarty to see that, you wouldn't get it. We already have hope and grounded optimism and generosity and virtue in abundance. You really don't get it, huh? Learning from other people's mistakes is so easy, people do it all the time, copying role models isn't the most natural way of learning.

When in doubt, be cruel. I suppose I do play a game-theoretic game with people: do you play games or are you trustworthy?

Of course I know what love is, of course I know. What about me suggests I don't? Apart from all actually loving people disliking me for some reason because they just don't get the depth of my selfless, otherworldly love?

I don't want power. I wish I had it, to make my problems go away and to impose my will on the world, make the internal and external consistent by even more means. Saying that is of course a way of making myself smaller, to reduce risk and responsibility, to make myself look selfless. And on the meta-level too and so on. I don't aim for those higher-order effects (presumptive effects?), I do just say what I believe is true. I don't know. (Wisdom allows to move beyond social constraints and is perhaps the only thing that should allow it? Not sure that second part is logically meaningful.) I think my actions show that I'm very genuine about my concerns. But all of that just creates more metrics to game. - I am a cautious person. My actions reveal my risk assessments, I don't do things I believe are risky.

I've tried writing more explicitly positive content. But I can't do it well, it's forced and hence useless. There's enough of that kind of writing, which leaves you with virtually invisible dissonance because it's a distortion of truth. Yes, that world would be better, if it were true. If those moves worked. And I suppose they work well enough for most people, I'm just really sensitive. That's somewhat self-congratulatory, I think that sensitivity is closely related to spiritual aptitude and that's of course what makes you a worthy person.

If I'm repeating myself: yes. Also, full anesthesia has side effects apparently. And I don't care, it's what's on my mind. I'm always in decline.

text:
There is some heaviness, dreariness, defeated-ness here. Like I said, I'm missing inspiration. And I feel restricted in unpredictable manners. Too much filtering, too much concern. Let's see how it'll all evolve.

I wish I knew how much my previous fifteen years mattered for my progress. Was it just dissecting every thought and impulse, accepting a lot of shadow intellectually, lots of self-reflection? Or were there necessary steps that I didn't realize happened? Like the initial break at the start of puberty, how big a deal is that usually? Is it possible and maybe even easy to induce on purpose? What exactly happened there?

Lack of mental tension seems like what people would consider head awakening? Anyway. Getting lack of emotional and sensational tension seems like the next steps. Mental tension seems to be the discrepancy between what is and what's desired or expected. (Is there an actual difference between wanting and expecting, or are these just two perspectives on the same phenomenon?) Lack of sensational tension would mean that physical pain becomes tolerable, or rather that toleration ceases to be a question.

If I'm not reasonable, everyone will go nuts.

I feel like I'm always teetering at the edge of just ending it finally but I also always have something more I want to do, something I want to understand or see. Once there's no more mystery, nothing I feel I still need to do, I'll quickly decay. Don't tell me the secrets! I wanna learn on my own. I can fill the holes later, if it becomes prudent to do so. But for now, it's for myself.

I don't say what I think I should believe, I say what I think I do believe.
